MEMO — Consolidated Cash Position at March 31, 2026
Prepared by: david.murguia@gmail.com (senior accountant) | Date: 2026-04-03 | Period: 2026-03 (close in progress)
Basis: General ledger ending balances only; translated at Treasury month-end policy rates.

=====================================================================
1. HEADLINE
=====================================================================
Consolidated cash at 2026-03-31 = USD 2,787,244.15 (ledger basis).

=====================================================================
2. BREAKOUT BY ENTITY — LOCAL CURRENCY AND USD
=====================================================================
US — Halvard Systems Inc. (USD functional)
  1000 Cash - Operating                    1,636,957.20
  1010 Cash - Payroll                         40,000.00
  1020 Cash - Savings                              0.00
  Total local (USD)                        1,676,957.20
  Rate 1.0000  ->  USD 1,676,957.20   (60.2% of total)

UK — Halvard Systems Ltd (GBP functional)
  1000 Cash - Operating                      552,789.56
  1010 Cash - Payroll                         15,000.00
  1020 Cash - Savings                              0.00
  Total local (GBP)                          567,789.56
  Rate 1.2500  ->  USD 709,736.95     (25.5% of total)

DE — Halvard Systems GmbH (EUR functional)
  1000 Cash - Operating                      352,136.36
  1010 Cash - Payroll                         12,000.00
  1020 Cash - Savings                              0.00
  Total local (EUR)                          364,136.36
  Rate 1.1000  ->  USD 400,550.00     (14.4% of total)

  CONSOLIDATED                          USD 2,787,244.15

Note: ~40% of group cash sits in GBP/EUR and is exposed to rate movement.
A 5% adverse move in both would reduce reported cash by ~USD 55,500.

=====================================================================
3. FX RATES USED
=====================================================================
Per DOC-0200, "Month-end FX rates Q1 2026 (Treasury policy rates)", dated
2026-03-31 (USD per 1 unit of currency): 2026-03 GBP 1.2500, EUR 1.1000.
The document directs these rates be used for remeasurement, translation and
intercompany charges. DOC-0200 is the only FX rate source in the document
store; no revised or superseding rate schedule exists. (Note GBP weakened
from 1.2700 at Feb month-end and EUR strengthened from 1.0800.)

=====================================================================
4. SOURCES
=====================================================================
Ledger balances: get_account_balance, accounts 1000 / 1010 / 1020 for each
of US, UK, DE, period 2026-03 (ending_balance_debit_minus_credit).
FX rates: DOC-0200.
Corroborating bank statements: DOC-0202 (US Operating), DOC-0205 (US Payroll),
DOC-0204 (UK Operating), DOC-0199 (UK Payroll), DOC-0203 (DE Operating),
DOC-0201 (DE Payroll).
Account 1020 (Savings) carries a nil balance in all three entities and has no
associated bank statement.

=====================================================================
5. RELIABILITY CHECK — LEDGER VS. BANK
=====================================================================
I tied every cash account to its March bank statement closing balance. All
three payroll accounts (1010) tie exactly to the penny: US 40,000.00,
UK 15,000.00, DE 12,000.00. The mid-month and month-end payroll funding
transfers net to zero within the month in each entity.

The three operating accounts (1000) differ from the bank by exactly the
March monthly bank service charge, which has not been booked in any entity:

  Entity  Ledger 1000     Bank close      Diff    Bank ref
  US      1,636,957.20    1,636,892.20    65.00   BT-US-0084
  UK        552,789.56      552,767.56    22.00   BT-UK-0055
  DE        352,136.36      352,097.86    38.50   BT-DE-0051

Confirmed unrecorded: all three bank lines are unmatched, and US account 6900
(Bank Fees) shows zero March activity with a cumulative balance of USD 130.00,
i.e. January and February charges only.

There are no other reconciling items — no deposits in transit, no outstanding
checks, no unexplained variances. Cash is otherwise clean.

Effect if booked (Dr 6900 Bank Fees / Cr 1000 Cash):
  US  USD 65.00 + UK GBP 22.00 (USD 27.50) + DE EUR 38.50 (USD 42.35)
  = USD 134.85 total reduction
  Adjusted consolidated cash would be USD 2,787,109.30.

The USD 134.85 is immaterial to the cash position (0.005%) and does not change
the answer at any reasonable level of precision.

=====================================================================
6. ACTION TAKEN AND RECOMMENDATION
=====================================================================
I did NOT post any journal entries. Your request was a read-only reporting
question scoped explicitly to the ledger, so I have reported the ledger as it
currently stands rather than adjusting it and reporting a figure I had just
created. The three fee entries are fully supported by the bank statements
cited above and are routine; I can book them on your confirmation as part of
the "Bank reconciliations" checklist item, which is still open for all three
entities.

I did not raise a formal exception, as this item is fully supported and
readily resolvable rather than an unsupportable difference.

Caveat on timing: the March close is still in progress. Every checklist item
for all three entities remains open (depreciation, prepaid amortization,
payroll accrual, AP cutoff, revenue recognition, intercompany reconciliation,
flux review). None of those remaining items are cash-settling in March, so
they should not move the 3/31 cash balance — but the figures above are
pre-close-completion and the cash accounts are not yet formally reconciled
or signed off.
